blocks.section: Parātrīśikāvivaraṇa
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta discovers that the universe has sixteen subdivisions of a breath, fifteen lunar days, a sixteenth power of emission, a seventeenth Goddess made from half of half a letter, and-because apparently that wasn't enough-some scriptures recognize an eighteenth. A philosopher objects that you cannot cut an indivisible phoneme into quarters. Abhinavagupta replies that the entire universe is indivisible consciousness, the objection collapses, and a Sanskrit grammar lesson somehow becomes an explanation of why you can hear sorrow in a voice before understanding a single word.
